recipes.name: New York Italian Pizza Dough
ingredients_raw: 2.5 cups warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)
0.25 cup bread flour, or more if needed

steps.text: Pour the warm water into the pan of a bread machine, sprinkle in the salt, and add the flour to the pan so the flour sits on top of the water. Make a hole in the top of the flour, and spoon the yeast into the hole. Let the mixture sit for 20 minutes to moisten the flour. Set the bread machine to the knead setting, and knead the dough for about 10 minutes. Turn the dough out onto a floured surface, and knead in 1/4 cup more flour or as needed, adding the flour about 2 tablespoons at a time, to make a wet, sticky, but elastic dough. The dough should be "as soft as a baby's bottom." Form the dough into a round shape.

Wipe the inside of a large bowl with olive oil, and place the round ball of dough into the bowl. Turn the dough over a couple of times so the dough picks up a thin coating of oil. Cover with a cloth, and refrigerate the dough for 10 hours or overnight.
The next day, allow the dough to come to room temperature before rolling out on a floured surface and adding toppings as desired. Roll the dough out thin with a thicker edge before adding toppings.

Place a pizza stone into oven, dust it with a little flour, and preheat oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C). Bake the pizza on the stone in the preheated oven until the bottom of the crust is browned, 6 to 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: New York Italian Pizza Dough
raw_recipe.description: Real New York-style pizza crust is chewy, thin, a little flexible, and dotted with bubbles and charred spots from the intense heat of the brick ovens. This version is kneaded in the bread machine, and develops complex, yeasty flavors from an overnight rise in the refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: This is the best pizza dough recipe I have found. I only let it sit in the refrigerator about 30 mins. and it still turned out really yummy!! I also used a mixer instead of my bread machine. I just find it easier! Thanks for this recipe, I love it!!

I halved the amount of ingredients, I was able to make two 12" pizzas. I did it by hand. Proofed the yeast in warm water then added all the other ingredients except for the oil for greasing the bowl later. It's hard to mix and knead this because the dough kept on sticking to my hands but because I added a little flour every now and then (as little as possible), I was able to reach the desired dough elasticity and softness without losing the high dough hydration. 

The extra work paid off. The crust was soooo good. It's the best pizza crust I've ever made! Crispy outside and chewy inside. It cooks really well on my home oven and air fryer. I added a 1/2 teaspoon of white sugar to the dough just to help with the browning since I didn't have a pizza stone. I used the metal tray that my oven came with and cranked up the temperature to the highest setting (446°F/230°C) to make the crust crispy outside.

The pizza flavor that I made was garlic and cheese with truffle salsa (minced porcini mushroom and black truffle with olive oil, brand is Mazza). I heated up a bit of EVOO then partially cooked the garlic. I hand stretched the pizza dough straight from the refrigerator. Topped it with crushed tomatoes with dried oregano, pinch of sugar and a little of olive oil. Sprinkled grated parmesan cheese, topped it with the slightly cooked garlic and low hydration mozzarella cheese. Cooked it in my convection oven at 230°F for 12 mins, added the truffle salsa on top, then cooked it again for

I’ve been trying every dough recipe I can to find one that makes a thin, crisp crust. This is it. I used my stand mixer: added yeast to water with a pinch of sugar. Let proof 10 minutes, then added the salt. Added 4 cups bread flour and gently mixed by hand, then let it sit for 15 minutes to let the flour hydrate. I kneaded for 15 minutes. It was wet, sloppy and messy! I added the last 0.5 cup of flour and mixed it in. I turned it out onto a floured board and kneaded for a few minutes. I placed the dough in an oiled bowl, covered it, and let it rise for an hour. I placed it in the fridge for 3-4 hours, punched it down, and let it warm on the counter. I pulled a small ball of dough, stretched it out very thinly, sauced it, and baked at 500F for 10 minutes. It was unbelievable how crisp and crunchy the crust was!

Delicious! Made exactly as per recipe, but I don't have a pizza stone, so I baked it off in a pre-heated cast iron skillet at 500 deg. Chewy crust, soft middle, crisp on bottom. The next day I pinched off pieces of raw leftover dough and fried them in my trusty cast iron skillet then tossed the fried dough in cinnamon sugar. Holy moly delicious!

This is by far the best pizza dough recipe that I have ever made. I make this ahead of time in a heavy duty mixer. I then divide the dough into four separate portions, put each portion in a 1 quart freezer Zip Lock bag, label and freeze. the night before I am going to make pizza, I put one of the portions in the refrigerator to thaw overnight. I then roll the dough out on a heavily floured surface, sprinkle more flour on the top of the dough to keep it from sticking and roll out to a medium size pizza, slightly larger than the pizza peal. Sprinkle corn meal on the pizza peal to keep the pizza dough from sticking to it. Roll the dough around a rolling pin so that it will keep its shape and roll back out onto the pizza peal. Press the dough to shape and bring the edges up slightly to hold the sauce. Spread sauce out evenly and top with your favorite toppings. I cooked the pizza on a preheated pizza stone in a convection oven at 525 degrees for 9 minutes. Let cool for a few minutes before slicing.

Beautiful!! Prepared this today in my kitchen aid mixer. Kept reminding myself that the batter will be very sticky. Proofed the yeast in one cup of the water adding a Tablespoon of sugar. After it proofed, I poured it into the mixing bowl adding the rest of the liquid ingredients. Replaced the beater with the dough hook & gradually added the rest of the flour kneading on speed 2 for another 8 minutes. I did add more flour than the recipe called for.This dough will not clean the sides of the bowl. It will look like a very thick pancake batter. On a heavily floured board I emptied my sticky dough. I kneaded it adding more flour until it barely held its shape. Placed it in an oiled bowl rotating it so the oil covered all of it. Into the fridge it went covered with a towel. Next day I removed it from the fridge and punched it down. Left it on the counter for about 3 hrs to take the chill out. I was detained & could not work on it as planned so I punched it down as it rose. Had to do this twice till I finally was able to shape it by patting it onto my pans & bake it. I had the oven preheated to 450 & semi baked the crusts for 9 min. on lowest rack. After cooling the crusts, I froze all of them except for one...my tester. I topped it with sauce & cheese. Into a 450 oven for about 12 min. on the lowest rack. Oh, I did add 1 Teas. of Garlic Powder & dried basil to the flour before mixing. That sticky dough rivals a tasty authentic Pizza even without a Pizza Stone. Thank you.

I made a triple batch for a pizza party. We used 7oz portions, and I had help making the crusts. Everyone who helped handle the dough thought it was sticky and hard to work with. I had no problems because I had a layer of flour under the dough and on my hands as I gently pressed the dough into a round. Everyone agreed that the cooked pizzas were wonderful, soft and puffy but still chewy. 
 I made this using a kitchen aid that usually struggles to make bread dough. It had no problems with this dough. You keep mixing till the gluten is developed and dough forms a rope of dough when you touch it and pull out.

I was worried I messed this up the first time when it poured out of my kitchen aid mixer like soupy dough, but with some flour and care, this is the best dough I’ve made for pizza. I’ve split this recipe in half to make thinner crust, but it makes a very chewy and thick crust on a 16 inch pan if you use the whole thing (very thick). I also prebake the crust for 3-4 minutes before topping. Seems to help. I butter the crust about 2/3 of the way into baking it with the topping on, also a nice touch.

Great! This was exactly what I was looking for. I halved recipe for 1 large pizza. I added 1/2tsp garlic powder, 1/4tsp onion powder, 1/4tsp oregano & basil to flour. I used a hand mixer with one dough hook, cuz I could only find one, lol. I refrigerated about 1 hour, rolled out and topped with "Exquisite Pizza Sauce" from this site(minus anchovy & honey), pepperoni, ham, mushrooms & mozzarella. I baked at 450 for 15 minutes on metal pizza pan. Delicious!! Soft and slightly chewy! Thanks for the recipe!!

Great basic recipe for the bread machine. Thanks. To take it one step further...add in to the bread machine... smells great even when the dough is rising in the machine....
3 crushed garlic cloves
2 tbs dried basil
2 tbs oregano
1/3 c Parmesan (yes in the dough)
1 tsp dried red pepper flakes 
Sounds like a lot of spices but when you are topping the crust with even more flavours it's nice to have the crust flavour come through

I make mine WITHOUT a bread machine, and it turns out wonderful. I use the same ingredients listed, though I might add up to a cup more flour depending on the humidity, b/c like the recipe states, this IS very sticky dough. To make by hand, I mixed the yeast and water to proof. Then I added the salt, a tsp or two of sugar (that's my only addition), and mixed in the flour until it was able to be turned out onto a floured surface for kneading. I kneaded for 5-10 minutes. Like the recipe states, the dough will be sticky, so I add just enough flour so that it's able to be handled but that it's also not a "stiff" dough. It should be very pliable and soft like a baby's bottom, like the submitter stated ;-) Then I patted it with oil and let it rise (about 1 hour). I then punched it down and made it into 2 crusts; one 10" round pan and one for a 11x13" rectangle sheet. This dough is easily "tossed" and stretched, so have fun with it! **I prebaked our crusts for about 8 minutes on 450°, until they barely started to have golden edges. Then I topped them and baked for about 10 more minutes, until it "looked" done. The center of our pizzas had a thin, chewy crust, and the big outside edges were delicious with a slight crisp outside, and chewy center. Yum!! Next time I'll get some nacho cheese to use as a dip for our crusts, which were tastier than breadsticks IMO:-) I definitely recommend this dough, it's simple and delicious.

Ok. I'm am leaving this review before actually making a pizza. My dough is currently sitting in the fridge overnight. I wanted to post my review on the recipe itself. The measurements are way off. Following the prescribed measurements, it is the consistency of batter, not dough. I had to add probably 2 more cups of flour to get it to a very sticky consistency. I don't know how others didn't have this issue. I will update my review after a pizza is made.

made it with AP flour in bread maker as stated. After taking out of bread machine, I rubbed surface of ball with olive oil and let it rest. Made lots of dough for a large 16" round pizza with a medium thick crust. Cooked pizza crust had the right chew and pretty good but needed some "taste". Maybe a bit more salt? oil? needs something.... It can be rolled thinner and baked in a rectangular sheet pan. I will try that next and I will oil the sheet pan before putting in the dough. Will make again,

This pizza dough is by far the best one I've tried. It is sticky and I won't lie can be hard to work with but once you master the art of rolling out pizza dough you'll be fine. Delicious and am waiting for mine to finish rising to have another
Really good. I do it in a stand mixer. I’ve made this twice now and both times I’ve had to add quite a bit more flour.

This is it!!!! Amazing... perfect... I’ve been searching for a dough recipe similar to all the small pizzerias, with that basic yummy chewy dough.. Found it!!!! The dough will be very wet and sticky. Don’t give up, Don’t freak out... Just add the extra flour at the end like it says. Just follow the directions.. You MUST make sure the dough is room temperature before rolling or stretching... I would recommend if your oven doesn’t go over 500 degrees, do 8 minutes at 500 degrees then turn on the broiler until you feel it’s browned enough. Great dough!!!! Thank you!!

When we make this dough, we always make an extra batch for the freezer because our kids love it so much. Yes, it's sticky. It's supposed to be. But it is the closest thing to NYC pizza dough I've found in Minnesota. Thanks so much - our kids (who are older, by the way) beg for homemade pizza night now, knowing that they'll have extras to make their own pizzas later.
Best dough I’ve ever made! I made mine a blender instead of a bread machine and it came out perfect.
Use this recipe to make 6 personal sized pizzas, and let the family add their own toppings.

Love this dough, sticky but end result excellent! Thanks to the previous review for making it by hand, works great.
DJ
